name: MARRIAGE (NEPALI)
description: Marriage is a three-pack Rummy game popular in Nepal (especially Kathmandu valley) and Bhutan, and by the Nepali diaspora. Played with 156 cards (three standard 52-card decks), each player receives 21 cards. Wild cards (tiplu, poplu, jhiplu) are determined during play. Players form sets of three: tunnela (three identical cards), pure sequence (three consecutive same suit), or trial (three same rank, different suits); the first to complete three pure sets chooses the tiplu (main wild). The first to arrange all cards into valid sets and discard wins the hand; scoring uses maal points and payments.

content.text: Marriage is a three-pack Rummy game popular in Nepal (especially Kathmandu valley) and Bhutan, and by the Nepali diaspora. Played with 156 cards (three standard 52-card decks), each player receives 21 cards. Wild cards (tiplu, poplu, jhiplu) are determined during play. Players form sets of three: tunnela (three identical cards), pure sequence (three consecutive same suit), or trial (three same rank, different suits); the first to complete three pure sets chooses the tiplu (main wild). The first to arrange all cards into valid sets and discard wins the hand; scoring uses maal points and payments.

Marriage is a three-pack Rummy game popular in Nepal, especially in the Kathmandu valley, and also played in Bhutan. It is widely played during the two main Hindu festivals Dashain (Dushera) and Tihar (Deewali) and by enthusiasts throughout the year.
Three standard 52-card packs shuffled together: 156 cards in all. No printed jokers; wild cards are created each deal (tiplu, poplu, jhiplu).
Three standard 52-card packs shuffled together: 156 cards in all. No printed jokers; wild cards are created each deal (tiplu, poplu, jhiplu).

Dealer gives 21 cards to each player. The next card is turned face up to start the discard pile; the rest form the face-down stock. Deal and play are clockwise in the most common rules; some regional rules use anticlockwise.

items.text: Direction of play: Some play anticlockwise with first card to dealer's right; many published rules and apps use clockwise.
Dhoos: Penalty (e.g. 15 points) for cheating or throwing maal to a player who has seen the tiplu; penalty cancelled if the offender wins the next hand.
Better: After rounds complete, play with double points; dublee can trigger better.
Open: Player may see the tiplu without laying three pure sets but may only use wilds after showing three pure sets.
